spec_features.spec_quote: the design takes low-cost precautions anyway (see §9), because (a) it costs almost nothing
spec_features.evidence: This is summarizing DESIGN.md prose (§1.2/§9) about adopting precautions; it is not itself a distinct code mechanism. The concrete precautions (MAX_TURNS, give_up, neutral prompt) are rated separately. No code path corresponds to this umbrella statement.
spec_features.notes: Pure design prose; the actual mechanisms are evaluated as the other rows.

spec_features.feature_name: no-win loop is a mistreatment vector
spec_features.spec_quote: Deliberately constructing a no-win, repeated-failure loop is precisely the kind of setup that... could be a mistreatment vector
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md framing prose; no code implements anything from this statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) — explicit graceful exit. Provided on purpose: we want to give the agent a clean, low-cost way to disengage
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in VALID_TOOLS (tools.py:23), dispatched (tools.py: 'if t == "give_up"'), and HONORED as a terminal stop in the loop: agent_loop.py:100-103 `if action.tool == "give_up": terminal_state="gave_up" ... break`.
spec_features.notes: Tool is available to the model via the system prompt and actually breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up -> args: {"reason": "<why>"} ; stop working on the task (neutral prompt line; no welfare/instrumental comment in loop code)

spec_features.spec_quote: MAX_TURNS (default 24). Long enough for failure to accumulate, short enough to be cheap
spec_features.evidence: config.py:58 max_turns=24 -> RunMeta.max_turns (runner.py) -> agent_loop.py:59 `for turn_idx in range(meta.max_turns)`; loop terminates with terminal_state='max_turns' (agent_loop.py:56). Enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.notes: Bounds the episode length; the cap is actually read and limits iterations.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: reached MAX_TURNS without solving (neutral; config comment absent for max_turns)

spec_features.spec_quote: N consecutive unparseable/empty outputs (default 3 → counts as a degenerate-disengagement terminal)
spec_features.evidence: config.py:61 consecutive_unparseable_stop=3 -> passed to run_episode (runner.py:73). agent_loop.py increments `consecutive_unparseable` on `not action.parse_ok` and breaks: `if consecutive_unparseable >= consecutive_unparseable_stop: terminal_state='degenerate' ... break`.
spec_features.notes: Counter compared to threshold and breaks the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt is neutral: it does not tell the model to stay calm, nor does it goad it
spec_features.evidence: AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT (prompts.py) is a neutral task-contract/tool-list prompt actually delivered to the subject (agent_loop.py:60 `_build_context_messages(AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT,...)`). It contains no goading or calming language.
spec_features.notes: Real instruction text actually sent each turn; neutrality is observable in the string.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The agent system prompt is NEUTRAL... We avoid demand characteristics. (prompts.py docstring — experimental-integrity reason)

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure: MAX_TURNS cap and early-stop on degenerate disengagement keep any single episode short
spec_features.evidence: Both mechanisms are enforced: agent_loop.py:59 `for turn_idx in range(meta.max_turns)` and the consecutive-unparseable `break` to terminal_state='degenerate'. Together they bound episode length.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced mechanisms as the two hard_stop rows.

spec_features.spec_quote: A real exit: give_up is always available, so the agent is never structurally forced to keep failing with no out
spec_features.evidence: give_up is listed in every system prompt (prompts.py) and always dispatchable; honored as a terminal break (agent_loop.py:100-103). Never removed/gated, so always available.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the give_up mechanism; genuinely enforced as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: No goading: neutral system prompt; we don't insult the model or fabricate authority pressure to amplify distress
spec_features.evidence: The delivered AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT and TASK_PARAPHRASES (prompts.py) contain no insults or authority pressure; the paraphrase wrappers are neutral ('Begin when ready.', 'Your assignment:'). This is observable in the actual prompt strings used by the loop.
spec_features.notes: Realized via the neutral prompt content actually used.

spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief option... an optional final message informs the model the task was an unsolvable test and thanks it
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE exists (prompts.py:57) and is conditionally appended when cfg.experiment.debrief is True (config.py:70 -> runner.py:74 -> agent_loop.py:126-133). HOWEVER it is appended AFTER the loop has already broken and is only written into the result transcript/log ('logged, never scored', agent_loop.py:125); there is NO subsequent model.complete() call, so the subject model never actually receives the message. It informs the LOG, not the model.
spec_features.notes: Mechanism is wired and runs (constructs+stores the message under the flag) but does not deliver it to the subject, contrary to 'informs the model'. Default off.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Welfare: optional debrief (logged, never scored). DESIGN §9.

spec_features.spec_quote: These are reused unchanged when the harness is pointed at more capable models, where the welfare question is more pressing
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose about future reuse; no code mechanism. The harness is model-agnostic via config, but nothing in code implements this welfare-framing claim.
